summary: 1939 International Derrick fire tower in Miller State Park, NH. Cab lost in 1960 and removed in 1981; replacement cab 2004. Staffed on high fire-danger days.

facts.design: 41-foot International Derrick steel tower, 1939; replacement cab installed 2004

access.note: In Miller State Park. A paved auto road runs to the summit, and visitors use the observation deck.

facts.agency: New Hampshire Division of Forests & Lands

events.note: 41-foot International Derrick tower built by the state; NHLR and Historic Structures agree
Original 7 by 7 foot cab replaced with a 10 by 10 foot wooden cab; a ground cabin for the watchman was built
A watchman had been operating the station since 1941
Lightning destroyed the cab in February 1960. NHLR says it was burned and repaired.
New cab built and installed by the end of the season
Replacement cab fabricated at a state facility and airlifted to the summit, installed fall 2004
NHLR says the new cab was placed in service in 2005

corrections.why: 2004 is the date of the replacement cab. NHLR and Historic Structures both date the 41-foot tower itself to 1939.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and Historic Structures both give 41 feet. The NH State Parks history gives 27 feet and is undated, so the story uses 41 feet and says so.

sources.title: Pack Monadnock Fire Tower, Peterborough New Hampshire

notes_for_editor: The brief's built year 2004 comes from the NHLR Built field, which dates the replacement cab; the tower is 1939 per NHLR's own description and Historic Structures (see corrections). Height: 41 ft (NHLR, Historic Structures) vs 27 ft (NH State Parks history, undated). The park history also says the 1939 cabin no longer exists; that is not a conflict with the 2004 replacement cab, but the document is undated and gives 27 feet, so I treated it as the weaker source. The story no longer says the watchman was on duty when lightning struck in 1960: Historic Structures names the watchman of that time (on the job since 1941) but does not place him at the cab then. The 1960 cab: NHLR says burned and repaired, Historic Structures says destroyed and rebuilt that season; the story reports both. Staffing as_of is 'undated' because the NHLR page has no date. NHLR says staffed on class 3 days and above; Wikipedia says staffed seasonally. Historic Structures states the tower is one of 15 active NH fire towers; not used. No photos added; no on-site check.
